Six Balls
5:00 AM. The maidan is grey and empty. Except for one old man and one tyre.
Heard about your little bet. Idiot. Pads on anyway.
You brought the tyre. Good. Now hang it from that tree and hit it straight. Five hundred times.
By the four-hundredth, your bat finally comes down straight. Your arms are on fire.
Vikrant has pace. Not brains. You want to know his secret, I can tell you. But nothing in my nets is free.
Ask for Pandey-ji's secret.
Read his bowling better in the duel.
"I'll figure him out myself."
Trust your eyes.
Hm. Pride. Expensive habit.
Watch his wrist, not the ball. When he's going short, his wrist flicks down early. Every time. Since he was nine.
Good luck chaiwala 🏏
Remember. Make him angry. He bowls short.
Also don't die. I need that interview.
By 4 PM, half of Rajgarh is at the maidan. Somebody is selling samosas. Somebody is taking bets.
Look at this crowd, chaiwala. All here to watch you cry.
"Bowl fast. It'll be over faster — for you."
Make him angry. More short balls.
Say nothing. Take guard.
Stay focused.
You say nothing. Vikrant's grin slips, just slightly.
Over faster? I'll put this ball through your helmet.
Vikrant Chauhan, full run-up. Survive all six and the maidan is yours. Get out and you never come back.
Six balls. Still standing. For two full seconds, the maidan is completely silent. Then it explodes.
FLUKE! That was a fluke!
Saturday. Club match against Meerut Lions. You're batting at four. Don't be late. Which means—
Early.
The stumps are on the ground. Somebody laughs. Then everybody does.
Bye-bye chaiwala! Go make me a cutting chai!
Saturday. Club match. Twelfth man. You carry the drinks.
Drinks. In front of the whole town.
Carry them like you're carrying the World Cup. Someone is always watching.
Dusk. You're packing your kit when a man in a safari suit sits down on the bench next to you.
Nice batting. Very nice. Listen, beta. District trials list is being made. Thirty-two boys. Sixteen places.
Chauhan sahab says ₹25,000 for a confirmed slot. Everyone pays. Don't be a hero.
Secretly record him on your phone.
Evidence. Could be dangerous.
"I don't have ₹25,000."
Honest.
"Get lost."
Proud.
Nobody has ₹25,000, beta. Ramesh-ji lends to everyone. Think about it. You have till Monday.
Your thumb finds the red button inside your pocket. 00:01. 00:02. 00:03...
...twenty-five thousand, cash, to Chauhan sahab's office. Monday. Don't be a hero, beta.
Got it. Every word.
It's raining. You get home. The stall's shutter is half down. Two motorbikes are parked outside, engines running.
Sunday was yesterday, Satish ji.
One of them has Papa by the collar.
Ramesh-ji's men are at the stall. And Papa is alone.
